title: [LANTR] Scalus: Multiplatform Tx Builder – same code for front&backend

ms.promise:
Scala 3 Cardano Transaction Builder API and domain classes based on Conway CDDL definitions.
It's a Scala/Java API, not a REST API, so no TPS measurement can't be done. So here we provide a list of requirements for the API.
API expected to be similar to Lucid Evolution and Cardano Client Lib libraries to simplify adoption by users.
API should allow
・construct all types of transactions:
・spending, 
・minting, 
・using native and Plutus scripts, 
・staking, 
・governance
・serialize/deserialize transactions
・balance transactions
・calculate fees and script execution budgets

In Milestone 1 the API methods won't yet have platform specific implementations, so most functionality can not be functionally tested.
Instead, we'll prepare a set on unit tests that should fail in M1 but should pass after platform specific implementations after M2 for JVM (using Cardano Client Lib implementation) and M3 on JavaScript (using Lucid Evolution implementation).

ms.report:
Transaction Construction and Serialization
We've implemented all the Conway Transaction types and CBOR serialization code:
https://github.com/nau/scalus/tree/v0.11.0/scalus-core/shared/src/main/scala/scalus/cardano/ledger
according to the Conway CDDL file: https://github.com/IntersectMBO/cardano-ledger/blob/master/eras/conway/impl/cddl-files/conway.cddl
For example TransactionBody type with its CBOR serialization logic: https://github.com/nau/scalus/blob/387cc25db4a0db8e2822086ddbdd187e265c0e76/scalus-core/shared/src/main/scala/scalus/cardano/ledger/TransactionBody.scala
Property-based tests covering serialization/deserialization roundtrip (isomorphism) using arbitrary instances of the Conway data types:
https://github.com/nau/scalus/blob/387cc25db4a0db8e2822086ddbdd187e265c0e76/scalus-core/shared/src/test/scala/scalus/cardano/ledger/CborSerializationTest.scala
The serialization logic and tests works on all 3 platfroms: JVM, JavaScript and Scala Native.
Transaction Builder API
This is our current Tx builder API:
https://github.com/nau/scalus/blob/74b8c9e7dd43884b0b534b33494a79a940118f0d/scalus-cardano-ledger/shared/src/main/scala/scalus/cardano/ledger/txbuilder/TxBuilder.scala
All the public API functions have a ScalaDoc comments.
This test covers creation of 5 different types of transactions (spend, mint, certificate, rewards, governance) using our first draft of Transaction Builder API:
https://github.com/nau/scalus/blob/badc5a3b5e666103e393528b19813d265b50f5b3/scalus-cardano-ledger/jvm/src/test/scala/scalus/cardano/ledger/txbuilder/TxBuilderComprehensiveTest.scala
Here is a PlutusScriptEvaluatorTest that:
・reads 3 Cardano mainnet blocks (11544748, 11544518, 11553070),
・deserializes from CBOR
・reads transactions
・evaluates scripts
・calculates their execution budgets
・validated the budgets they are correct.

In Milestone 2 we aim to implement the Tx Builder API on the JVM platform as described in our original funding proposal.
We are going to use the Bloxbean Cardano Client Lib Java library for transaction serialization, fee calculation and balancing, signing and transaction submission.
We'll make sure that the automated tests suits developed in Milestone 1 now pass, ensuring isomorphism of serialization/deserialization of at least 100 real mainnet transactions of different types (simple, with script execution, with governance).
We'll create an integration test suit that ensures that valid transactions are produced and can be successfully submitted using a local Cardano node using Yaci DevKit.

In Milestone 3 we aim to implement the Tx Builder API on the JavaScript platform as described in our original funding proposal.
We are going to use Anastasia Labs Lucid Evolution TypeScript library for transaction serialization, fee calculation and balancing, signing and transaction submission.
We'll make sure that the automated tests suits developed in Milestone 1 now pass, ensuring isomorphism of serialization/deserialization of at least 100 real mainnet transactions of different types (simple, with script execution, with governance).
We'll create an integration test suit that ensures that valid transactions are produced and can be successfully submitted using a local Cardano node using Yaci DevKit.
